messages:
incident-bot: ALERT: canary error-rate spike detected on service:runtime-infer-canary (hosted). 5xx rate > 8% over 2m, latency tail increasing. Trigger: canary-deploy-2026-03-15. Auto-abort not configured.
jamie_oncall: oncall taking this. seeing 503s and OOM logs on a subset of nodes. looks related to new cache-evict optimizer in v2.3. toggled to 3% traffic canary earlier.
sara_prodeng: thanks. are the errors concentrated in a specific AZ or hw type? could be quantized-kernel mismatch.
jamie_oncall: checks: host labels show gpu-type:A100-split-quant on canary pool. errors spike on nodes with nv_switch toggled. logs: `runtime.core: kvcache evict: invalid pointer` repeated.
ops_pete: copying recent logs:
```
Mar 15 14:02:21 node-23 runtime: ERR kvcache evict: free invalid ptr 0x7f4c
Mar 15 14:02:21 node-23 kernel: oom-killer invoked
Mar 15 14:02:23 proxy: 503 upstream read timeout
```

nicole_support: customer-impact? any paid customers affected?
jamie_oncall: small % of hosted customers hitting canary nodes. 503s for generation requests longer than 10s. severity: P2 if contained, but trending. recommend immediate traffic rollback for canary and flip feature flag to safe.
ben_platform: we have a soft kill switch on feature flag service: `flags.redwood.internal/toggle`. can someone flip to `cache_optimize_v2:off`?
sara_prodeng: i'll flip the flag but let's also drain traffic from canary pool to be safe. jamie, can you run the drain command for the canary pool?
jamie_oncall: running now. command used:
```
# drain canary pool
rctl cluster drain --pool infer-canary-2026-03-15 --grace 30s
```

jamie_oncall: drain issued -> pool entering DRAINING. verifying proxy routing now.
ben_platform: flag toggle curl (for reference):
```
curl -X POST -H "Authorization: Bearer $OP_TOKEN" \
  -d '{"flag":"cache_optimize_v2","value":false}' \
  https://flags.redwood.internal/api/v1/toggle
```

sara_prodeng: I flipped cache_optimize_v2 -> off. ops_pete can you confirm flag propagation? (reacts: :eyes:)
ops_pete: flag propagated to all regions in ~12s. console shows OFF for all pids.
jamie_oncall: proxy routing now routing around drained nodes, 5xxs dropping on monitoring. current 5xx = 1.2% and falling. tail latency back within SLO.
alice_sre: starting smoke tests against hosted endpoints (100 reqs / 1k tokens). will post results in 2m.
nicole_support: posting to status page draft: "We are mitigating an issue impacting a small subset of Gen API requests. Traffic has been re-routed and a feature flag rolled back. We will provide updates in 30 minutes." Any objections?\sara_prodeng: go ahead. include that we’re investigating root cause and may revert canary changes after deeper look.
jamie_oncall: smoke tests baseline: 100 req -> 0 failures, median latency nominal. I propose we leave canary drained and keep flag off until next staged rollout.
ben_platform: agree. schedule: keep canary pool offline for 4 hours, collect core dumps and traces. will open internal ticket.
ops_pete: I'll collect node core dumps: command:
```
ssh node-23 'sudo gcore -o /var/tmp/core.node-23 `pgrep runtime`'
rsync /var/tmp/core* ops-logs:/mnt/infra/incident-1759992222/
```

jamie_oncall: assigning follow-ups: sara to own postmortem + flag rollback notes, ben to own infra traces, pete to archives, nicole to coordinate customer comms (sent initial status). I'll monitor for 60m then hand to next oncall unless things regress.
sara_prodeng: noted. I'll create postmortem draft with timeline and retention of canary artifacts.
ben_platform: tagging relevant kernel/quantization teams. cc: @quant-kernels @kernel-sheriffs.
alice_sre: smoke tests green. continuous metrics show stable for 5m. marking thread for watch.
nicole_support: status page updated, emailing impacted customers with initial blurb.
jamie_oncall: closing mitigation phase. leaving action items open. if anyone sees new spike ping pager. (reacts: :thumbsup:)
incident-bot: Incident note: mitigation completed at 1759992280. Metrics returned to baseline. Follow-up ticket: INF-2026-789 opened."
